explanations.answer: Cross to the other side of the sea
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus sees a large crowd around Him, and He gives orders to cross to the other side of the sea (Matthew 8:18). The text doesn't say why He gives the order, so I won't guess. I just know a crowd that big would have me hiding behind my cookie boxes.

explanations.answer: Send the crowd home for the night
explanations.explanation: Nice thought, friend, but that's not what the text says. Matthew 8:18 says Jesus gave orders to cross to the other side of the sea. Nothing there about sending anyone home. I once tried sending a crowd of hungry bakers home, and they just stood there looking at my cookies.

explanations.answer: Go up the mountain to pray
explanations.explanation: No mountain in this one, baker. When Jesus saw the large crowd, He gave orders to cross to the other side of the sea (Matthew 8:18). The sea is where this story is headed, and it gets a LOT busier out there.

explanations.answer: A place to lay His head
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker. Jesus says, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” (Matthew 8:20) Even a fox gets a den and a bird gets a nest. I know a little about not having a place to rest, because I spent years in the back of a drawer.

Close to the road, but not the one, friend. Jesus says the Son of Man has “no place to lay His head.” (Matthew 8:20) He doesn't say anything about friends. In fact, His disciples follow Him into the boat in verse 23.

Good guess, baker, but money never comes up. Jesus says foxes have dens and birds have nests, “but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” (Matthew 8:20) It's all about a place to rest. I'd say a coin is hard to hold onto anyway, and I only cost a quarter.

Careful there, baker, this one sneaks up on you. The disciple doesn't ask to say goodbye to his family. He says, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.” (Matthew 8:21) Goodbye and burying are two different requests, so the statement is false.

You've got it, baker. The disciple says, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.” (Matthew 8:21) He never asks about saying goodbye to his family. He calls Jesus Lord and asks to do one thing first, and the text says exactly what that one thing is.

explanations.answer: Follow Me and let the dead bury their own dead
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Jesus tells him, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” (Matthew 8:22) That's a tough one, and I think it's a heavy moment. The text doesn't give us more, so I'll leave it right where it is.

explanations.answer: Go bury your father and then return to Me
explanations.explanation: That's the answer a lot of us would hope for, friend, but it isn't what Jesus says. He tells the disciple, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” (Matthew 8:22) This is a heavy moment, and the text doesn't add anything else. So I won't either.

explanations.answer: Stay with your family until the mourning ends
explanations.explanation: That sounds gentle, baker, but it isn't in the text. Jesus tells him, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” (Matthew 8:22) Nothing about staying home or waiting for mourning to end. I think this one is a heavy moment, so I'll just stay with the words.
That's right, baker. The boat is engulfed by the waves, “But Jesus was sleeping.” (Matthew 8:24) Waves everywhere, and He's asleep. The only thing I've ever slept through was my own alarm clock.

Good guess, friend, but the text says something different. Matthew 8:24 says the boat was engulfed by the waves “But Jesus was sleeping.” Praying doesn't come up here. Sleeping, in the middle of all that.
Nope, nobody's at the wheel in this story, baker. Matthew 8:24 says the waves engulfed the boat, “But Jesus was sleeping.” The text doesn't say who was steering. It does say who was asleep.

explanations.answer: Save them because they are perishing
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The disciples go and wake Him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!” (Matthew 8:25) They call Him Lord and they ask Him to save them. Plain words, from people in a real panic.

explanations.answer: Turn the boat back toward the shore
explanations.explanation: Sensible plan, friend, but that's not what they say. The disciples wake Him with, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!” (Matthew 8:25) They ask Jesus to save them. Nobody mentions the shore.

explanations.answer: Help them bail the water out
explanations.explanation: It's a smart idea when a boat is filling up, baker. But the disciples don't ask for bailing help. They say, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!” (Matthew 8:25) Their request is to be saved.

That's right, baker. Jesus replies, “You of little faith, why are you so afraid?” (Matthew 8:26) He asks them why they are so afraid. I think that's a question worth sitting with, and I won't add more than the text gives.
Not this time, friend. Jesus does ask them. He replies, “You of little faith, why are you so afraid?” (Matthew 8:26) So the statement is true. He asks the question right after they wake Him.
Not quite, baker. The text says Jesus “rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm.” (Matthew 8:26) Perfectly calm means no rough water left. So the statement is false.
Yes, baker. After Jesus rebukes the winds and the sea, “it was perfectly calm.” (Matthew 8:26) Not a little rough, not mostly calm. PERFECTLY calm. My dough has never once behaved that well.
You've got it, baker. “The men were amazed” (Matthew 8:27). The sea is perfectly calm, and they're amazed. I think I would have been standing there with my mustache hanging open.
That's not what the text says, friend. “The men were amazed” (Matthew 8:27). Nothing about shame. The text gives their feeling right there, and it's amazement.
Offended, baker? The text says no. “The men were amazed” (Matthew 8:27). I don't think anyone gets offended by a calm sea after a violent storm. Amazed is the word.

explanations.answer: What kind of man is this
explanations.explanation: That's the question, baker. The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey Him!” (Matthew 8:27) They'd just seen the storm go quiet. I'd be asking questions too, probably with a trembling mustache.

explanations.answer: Where did this storm come from
explanations.explanation: Fair question for a storm that showed up out of nowhere, friend. But it isn't theirs. The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this?” (Matthew 8:27) They're asking about Jesus, not the storm.

explanations.answer: Why did He wait so long
explanations.explanation: That's a thought that might cross a mind, baker, but the text doesn't have it. The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey Him!” (Matthew 8:27) Their question is about who Jesus is. It isn't about timing.
